summaries.pv2: Slides 7–12 score 4/10 against the MBB-exec bar: the design shell (light canvas, wordmark band, indigo Poppins titles, accent-bar cards) is mostly in place, but the half is sunk by three critical defects — slide 8 renders half-empty (blank profile card, 'data not available' placeholder, and a contentless wrong-color takeaway band), the currency is bare '$' on a New Zealand plan and even mixes NZ$/$ within slide 9, and slides 7 and 12 leak an AI-training-client template (developer/writing-expert CPA taxonomy, 'AI Trainers' case study, a 'nurse-level CPAs' benchmark note) into an Aerospace & Defense deck. Add broken benchmark logic on slide 9 (identical values marked 'beating benchmark', a perfect 10.0/10 industry average) and takeaway bands missing on 4 of 6 slides, and the numbers-credibility and answer-first requirements both fail. Slide 11 shows the pipeline CAN hit the baseline; slides 7, 8, 9 and 12 need content regeneration with client context and NZD enforced, not just styling fixes.

summaries.ox: The workbook nails the Joveo skin — palette, Poppins/Inter, purple headers, freeze panes, no N/A, honest confidence ranges — but fails the enterprise bar on data integrity and editorial finish. Four critical defects would surface within minutes of a client read: the Exec Summary total row's SUM formulas are shifted one column left (the headline table totals '$1'); the Channel Recommendations sheet is a second, contradictory plan (4,882 apps at $49 CPA vs 12,755 at $19, spend summing to $240,240); the plan projects 143 hires against the client's stated 5,000-hire goal and even argues the budget is too big; and the ROI sheet's conversion assumptions disagree with its own projections by 5–10x. Around them sit ~150 cells of text-typed money, a mid-word 120-char truncation, 4,000-character snake_case dict dumps, 'pheonix' spelled wrong six times, a broken salary distribution (Min > P25, Min = Median = Max), ten-row boilerplate tables, and a validation banner claiming 7/7 checks passed. Ship-blocking as-is: fix the total row, delete or reconcile Channel Recommendations, address the 5,000-hire gap head-on, convert text metrics to numeric, and replace raw enrichment dumps with curated tables before any client sees it.
summaries.pc: The generated core is impressively self-consistent — budget, all 8 channel splits, 4,418 applies, 30 hires, and CPA/CPH match to the dollar between deck and workbook, and the arithmetic all checks out. But the bundle fails the two checks a client performs first: (1) the deck denominates the entire plan in NZD while the workbook labels the identical numbers USD (explicit 'Budget (USD)' header) — a ~39% ambiguity on every money figure in a plan that should be NZD throughout; and (2) the deck's channel-breakdown table silently drops Social Media and EMEA Regional but keeps the 8-channel totals, so its visible rows sum to NZ$142,500/4,335 apps against a printed NZ$150,000/4,418. Beyond those, the workbook carries a second contradictory projection (1,637 apps at $91.63 CPA on Channel Recommendations), a 50-100 hire goal vs 30 projected, three different salary medians for the same role, deck benchmarks (CPA, CPH, apply rate, CPC) that contradict the workbook's own benchmark sheet, a '75,000 active jobs' claim the workbook's demand table records as 0, and US-only niche boards/clearance content in an NZ plan. Fixing the currency labels and the slide-6 table would lift this to ~7; the benchmark and boilerplate cleanup is needed before this is client-safe.
summaries.oc: The budget spine of the Omada.ai bundle is tightly consistent — $240,000 total, the 40/22/20/8/7/3 six-channel split, 143 hires, 12,755 applications, and $18.82 CPA reconcile exactly between the deck (slides 2/5/6/10) and the workbook's Executive Summary, ROI, and 90-Day sheets, and currency is uniformly USD. But the audit found one critical defect: the workbook Executive Summary's Total row formulas are shifted one column left, so the client-facing first sheet displays Total budget '$1' and Projected Hires '12,755', directly contradicting the deck's correct totals. Beyond that, the workbook's Channel Recommendations sheet is effectively a second, conflicting plan (7 channels, 4,882 apps, $49.16 CPA vs 6 channels, 12,755 apps, $18.82), and the deck's market narrative contradicts the workbook's own data in five places: benchmark ranges (CPA/CPC/CPH/apply-rate all differ), CPC trend (+9.2% rising vs Stable), apply-rate framing ('above average' vs a 6-8% benchmark), salary ($95K degenerate range vs $75K city baseline), and live postings (180,000 claimed vs 0 recorded). Cost-per-hire also appears as both $1,678 and $1,675, and duration is stated as both 1-2 years and 90 days. Recommendation: fix the total-row formula shift, delete or clearly label the Channel Recommendations sheet as an alternative scenario, and regenerate the deck's benchmark panel from the workbook's benchmark rows before this bundle goes to a client. minors.where: Executive Summary B72 ('Overall: 45/100 (Grade F)'), B74, B79; Sources & Confidence B3 ('D')
minors.title: Plan grades its own inputs F/D on page one without framing
minors.detail: Creative Quality 45/100 Grade F with 'Description Length: 0/25 (currently ~0)' reveals the generator scored an empty job description and shipped anyway; overall data confidence 53% 'D' is the visual centerpiece of the Sources sheet. Honesty is good, but presented raw with no 'what we'll do about it' framing it reads as the vendor indicting its own product.

minors.where: Market Intelligence B3; Exec Summary B13:D14; Market Intelligence B39:G48
minors.title: Orphan/thin sections and mislabeled columns
minors.detail: 'National Economic Snapshot' (B3) is a header with no content under it. 'COMPANY INTELLIGENCE' on the Exec Summary contains a single generic row (Industry: Retail & Consumer). Location Intelligence's 'Key Industries' column actually lists employers (AT&T, MD Anderson, HCA Healthcare) — several healthcare-heavy lists that look imported from a healthcare dataset for a retail client; 3 of 10 cities are all-dash rows.

minors.where: Niche Board Matching C13/B19; Channels & Strategy B42
minors.title: 'RetailGigs' unverifiable and best-practice guidance conflicts with the plan
minors.detail: 'RetailGigs' does not correspond to a known job board (Snagajob/Wonolo/Instawork are real) — needs verification before a client sees it. The sheet also advises 'Allocate 10-20% of total budget to niche boards' while the plan allocates 8%.

minors.where: Executive Summary B22/B24 vs strategy: Social Media row
minors.title: 20% of budget parked on the plan's own worst channel
minors.detail: Social Media gets $48,000 (20%) for a projected 3 hires at $16,000/hire and ROI score 4/10, while Regional Boards ($0.67 CPC, ROI 10) get 7%. The Risk Analysis section discusses concentration risk but never addresses why a fifth of spend sits on a channel the model itself scores as failing — the kind of unforced strategic incoherence an MBB reviewer catches immediately.

minors.where: Deck slide 6 Total row ('101%') vs Workbook Executive Summary C22-C29 (sums to 100.2%)
minors.title: Deck's allocation percentages total a printed '101%'
minors.detail: Rounding each channel share up (31+21+16+13+11+4+3+2) produces a Total row that literally reads 101%. The workbook's underlying fractions sum to 100.2% and its own Total row (B30) is an empty label with no values at all. Cosmetic, but it sits on the money slide.

minors.where: Deck slide 7 'CPA Reference' (Backend/Frontend Developers $8-$14 ... Finance Analysts $13-$18)
minors.title: CPA reference slide is boilerplate for tech/AI-training roles, unrelated to the plan and in USD
minors.detail: The slide benchmarks developers, writers, CAD engineers and finance analysts at $8–$35 CPA — no aviation or trades role appears, none of the ranges relate to the plan's NZ$33.95 CPA, and the currency silently switches to USD. It reads as template residue from a different client and invites 'why is my CPA 2-4x these?' questions.

minors.where: Workbook Executive Summary D6 ('3-6 months') vs Deck slide 9 (Weeks 1-12) and 90-Day Forecast (Jul 1 - Sep 30)
minors.title: Campaign duration stated as '3-6 months' in workbook vs a 12-week plan everywhere else
minors.detail: The deck's implementation roadmap and the workbook's own 90-Day Forecast both describe a 12-week campaign; the Campaign Overview says '3-6 months'. Defensible as a range but loose next to two artifacts that commit to 90 days.

minors.where: Deck slide 2 RESOLUTION block vs slide 5 channel mix
minors.title: Executive summary lists only 5 of the 8 channels as the strategy
minors.detail: Slide 2's checkmarked strategy names Programmatic DSP, Global Job Boards, Niche/Industry Boards, Social Media and Regional Boards — omitting Employer Branding (13%, the 4th-largest allocation), APAC Regional and EMEA Regional — while calling it an '8-channel programmatic strategy' in the same block. Also 'Talent Profile: White Collar dominant (100%)' is a questionable classification for an aircraft tradesperson role, echoed by the workbook's 'Professional / White-Collar' tier.

minors.where: Workbook Executive Summary F9 ('5000 hires' Hire Volume) vs 143 projected hires everywhere else
minors.title: Workbook exposes a 5,000-hire volume goal the deck never mentions
minors.detail: The Campaign Overview lists Hire Volume '5000 hires' while the plan projects 143 hires (2.9% of the stated need). The deck omits the 5,000 figure entirely, so the artifacts tell different stories about hiring ambition vs delivery.

minors.where: Deck slide 7 (CPA Reference) vs Workbook retail benchmarks
minors.title: Deck CPA Reference slide is boilerplate for tech/AI-training roles, not this plan
minors.detail: Slide 7 lists Backend/Frontend Developers, Full Stack, CAD/Game Engineers, Computational Scientists and 'Finance Analysts (AI Training)' with $6-$35 CPA ranges — none relevant to a Business Sales Representative / Retail & Consumer plan, and disconnected from both the workbook's retail CPA benchmark ($8-$25) and the plan's channel CPAs ($11-$215). Slide 11's case study is likewise 'AI Trainers'.

minors.where: Deck slides 5/6/10 vs Workbook Exec Summary B22-B27 and Channels & Strategy B4-B9
minors.title: Channel naming drift and raw snake_case identifiers leak into client-facing text
minors.detail: Deck uses 'Global Job Boards' / 'Niche / Industry Boards' / 'Programmatic DSP'; workbook uses 'Global Boards' / 'Niche Boards' / 'Programmatic Dsp', and the Channels & Strategy sheet uses raw keys (programmatic_dsp, global_boards). Deck slide 10 also prints 'programmatic_dsp, global_boards' verbatim in the risk copy. Names map 1:1, so it is cosmetic, but polish suffers.

minors.where: Deck slide 2 RESOLUTION checklist
minors.title: Six-channel plan but the strategy checklist names only five channels
minors.detail: The checkmark list names Programmatic DSP, Global Job Boards, Niche/Industry Boards, Social Media, and Regional Boards, with the sixth checkmark being 'ML-optimized bidding across 10,238+ publishers'. Employer Branding — a funded channel at 3% ($7,200) on slides 5-6 — is missing from the list.

minors.where: Deck slide 2 COMPLICATION bullets vs entire workbook
minors.title: Deck-only market stats with no workbook support
minors.detail: '64,000 retail jobs shed in 2025 Q1', '5,800+ store closures', and '10,238+ publishers' appear only in the deck; no workbook sheet carries these figures (the only '64,000' hits in the workbook are unrelated salary values). Not a contradiction, but unverifiable from the bundle.

minors.where: Workbook Market Intelligence B27/B175, Quality Intelligence B10/B24, etc.
minors.title: 'pheonix' misspelling of Phoenix repeated across four workbook sheets
minors.detail: The location is spelled 'pheonix' in every workbook occurrence (Market Intelligence, Quality Intelligence, Geographic Cost Variance, per-role salary tables); most other city names are also lowercased ('houston', 'atlanta') while 'Dallas' is capitalized. The deck avoids the issue only because it never lists the cities.
